A release about words — the ones in your files, and the ones your files spell two different ways.
Built on [MangoTile 1.0.4](https://github.com/Diffechento/MangoTile/releases/tag/v1.0.4).

**Lyrics come off the device, and they follow the music.** A `.lrc` beside a song — the thirty-year-old
format every other player reads — is used ahead of anything fetched from the internet, and when it
carries timestamps the page keeps up with the track: the line being sung is the big one, the rest sit
back out of the way, and tapping any line jumps the song to it. A chorus written twice in the file
highlights in the right place each time round rather than always the first. Scroll the page by hand and
it stops chasing you for a few seconds, which is long enough to read back a verse.

**Words written inside the file are read too**, which is where a FLAC usually keeps them — and an MP3
and an M4A, under their own names for the same thing. Many of those tags hold a whole `.lrc` pasted in,
timestamps and all, so those follow the music exactly as a separate file does. Between a timed source
and a flat one the timed one wins, wherever each came from.

**You choose where the rest are looked up**, on settings → library: **LRCLIB** or **Genius**. They are
different things rather than two of the same. LRCLIB is a community collection of `.lrc` files and is
the only one of the two that can answer with *timings*, so a song with no file of its own can still
follow along; Genius reaches further into obscure and non-English catalogues and publishes words
without timings, which it has never had. Neither needs an account, and LRCLIB is the default. Fetched
words can be saved next to the song as a `.lrc`, so they outlive this app — off by default, since it is
the one lyrics setting that writes files to the phone.

**Full screen**, on settings → interface. The status bar goes away and every page — the library, the
player, a settings page — runs to the top edge of the screen, which is a big title's worth of height
back on a phone. Swipe down from that edge and the clock comes back over the page for a few seconds,
then leaves again by itself. Off by default: it is a mode to ask for rather than one to find yourself
in. The navigation bar stays where it is — the gesture pill is how you leave.

**Two files that spell one name differently are one artist.** `Молодой Платон` written with a
ready-made `й` and the same name written as `и` with a mark over it look identical and were two
artists with one track each, with nothing on screen to explain why. Names are brought to one encoding
before anything is compared, and a space, a hyphen or a dash between the same words is now a
difference in the tags rather than in the band — "Blink 182", "Blink-182" and "Blink‐182" are one
artist, keeping the spelling most of your files use.

**The artists section can be built from the album artist alone**, on settings → library, for libraries
where every other track is tagged "band, guest, guest, guest" and the list fills with names you have
one song by. And **a shared track can go to the artist you have most of** rather than to whoever the
tag happens to name first. Both are off by default: they are readings of your tags rather than what
the tags say.

**Albums on an artist's page can be ordered by name** instead of by year, on settings → interface. A
discography reads as a run of releases, so newest-first is still the default; someone who knows a
record by its title now has the alphabet instead.

**Fixed: editing an album's tags did nothing on files that carry the same field twice.** A rip that has
been through more than one tagger often has the album artist written under two or three names at once —
`ALBUMARTIST`, `ALBUM ARTIST`, `ALBUM_ARTIST` — and only one of them was being rewritten, so the album
went on showing the old artist and the edit looked as though it had not saved. The others are taken
with it now. The permission Android asks for before changing your music can also be given **once**
instead of once per album, from the edit page.

**Fixed: a song with no cover played behind the last song's artwork.** The band behind the mini player
kept the previous record's picture, because "still decoding" and "this album has no cover" reached it
as the same answer.

**Fixed: the cover flew across the screen if you moved a page before it landed.** Opening an album
sends its cover from the list to the page; scrolling before it arrived left it chasing the moving list
over the top of everything, the status bar included. A page that is turning now ignores the finger for
the quarter-second the turn lasts. That is framework work — MangoTile 1.0.4.

**Fixed: the line being sung changed over with a stutter**, and not because anything was dropping
frames — growing the text meant re-measuring it, so the page reflowed half way through. It is measured
once and only drawn larger now. Over the same seven line changes, frames longer than 30ms went from
twenty-nine to two.

---

Scrobbling, the online cover lookup, the queue and the equalizer are unchanged. The APK carries the
same signing certificate as every release since 1.0 (`SHA-256 494018a9…2acf7c09`), so it installs over
any of them as an update and keeps your settings, favourites, play counts and queue.

minSdk 26 · compileSdk 36 · GPLv3 · third-party notices are in the app, on settings → about.
